What pressure washing in Katy is up against

Katy grew out of flat coastal prairie. It started as Cane Island, opened its post office in 1896, and turned to rice after 1901. Texas's first concrete rice dryers went up here in 1944. Most of what people now call Katy came much later, as master-planned neighborhoods spread across the old fields, so pressure washing in Katy usually means wide driveways, brick-and-siding two-story homes and long runs of shared wood fence.

Open country brings wind, and wind brings dust. Soil splashes onto the lowest course of brick and the bottom siding boards every time a storm blows through, and the side of a fence that never sees sun turns green. In late winter and early spring, oak pollen settles on patios and cars. Summer flips the problem around: heat drives up water demand, and that can put limits on washing hard surfaces.

Which rulebook covers your Katy address?

Katy sits where Harris, Waller and Fort Bend counties meet, about 25 miles west of downtown Houston along I-10. A "Katy" mailing address can be inside the City of Katy, in Cinco Ranch, or in an unincorporated neighborhood served by its own water district. Before a summer wash, it helps to know which one you are.

Who sets water-use and exterior rules for different kinds of Katy addresses
Where you liveWater-use and drought rulesExterior standards
Inside the City of Katy (21,894 people in 2020)The City's drought contingency planCity code, plus your HOA if you have one
Cinco Ranch (16,899 people in 2020, Houston ETJ)The water provider named on your billThe Cinco Ranch associations' deed restrictions
Other neighborhoods outside city limits, in Harris, Fort Bend or Waller CountyThe water provider named on your billYour association's deed restrictions, if any

The quickest test: look at who sends your water bill. That provider's drought plan, not the City of Katy's, is usually the one that applies to your hose and to the company you hire.

Drought stages and a summer wash in Katy

The City of Katy's drought contingency plan names power washing directly. As conditions worsen, it asks residents to cut water used for power washing buildings, sidewalks, driveways, parking lots and other hard surfaces, and its stricter stages go further and restrict hosing down paved areas and buildings. The exact wording for each stage is in the City's code, so read the current version rather than relying on memory.

This is not theoretical. The City called Stage 2 and Stage 3 restrictions in recent summers, including 2022 and 2023, when heat pushed water demand up.

  1. Find your current stage. Check your water provider's website or bill insert. Inside city limits that is the City of Katy; elsewhere it is your district.
  2. Mention it on the call. Tell the company you are put through to which stage is in effect. It can say whether the job fits the rules now or should wait.
  3. Ask where the rinse water goes. Katy's Public Works department runs a stormwater program that takes reports of illicit discharges. Soapy water belongs on the lawn or in containment, not in the street inlet.
  4. Move the job if you can. If the cleaning is not urgent, a spring or fall date avoids planning around a summer stage at all.

Barker Reservoir and old flood lines

Some Katy neighborhoods carry a particular history. During Hurricane Harvey in 2017, water pooled behind Barker Reservoir and entered thousands of homes in parts of Cinco Ranch, Kelliwood and Canyon Gate. The Addicks and Barker dams were built in the 1940s to protect Buffalo Bayou, and in 2019 a federal judge found the government liable for flooding upstream of them.

Years later, a tide line can still show on a back fence, a garden wall or the lower brick of a garage. If you have one, describe it on the call. A company can look at whether it is a surface stain that cleaning can lighten or a mark that has gone into the material, and tell you honestly before you pay for anything.

Big associations and shared fences

Katy's large master-planned communities lean on deed restrictions to keep streets looking uniform. Cinco Ranch, for example, began in 1984 when a group of developers bought the ranch for a 5,000-acre planned community, and associations there enforce deed restrictions. Some associations also maintain perimeter and common-area fencing, including cutting back ivy and other growth. Before you hire anyone to clean a fence, confirm whether it is yours or the association's, and check your association's current rules on stain colors.

Services that matter most around Katy

  • Driveway cleaning: wide two- and three-car driveways show tire marks and the dark strip along the lawn edge first.
  • House washing: soft washing takes prairie dust and mildew off brick and siding without forcing water behind the boards.
  • Fence cleaning: the common target of HOA letters, and the surface most easily damaged by too much pressure.
  • Oil and rust stain removal: garage aprons collect oil drips, and fertilizer can leave orange spots that rinsing alone will not lift.
  • Commercial pressure washing: shops, offices and restaurants along the I-10 corridor, out toward Katy Mills (open since 1999), have sidewalks and dumpster pads to keep up.

Common questions

Can I get my driveway pressure washed in Katy during a drought stage?

It depends on which stage is in effect and who supplies your water. The City of Katy's drought plan names power washing of driveways, sidewalks and buildings among the uses it asks people to cut, and its tighter stages restrict hosing down hard surfaces altogether. Cinco Ranch and other addresses outside the city follow their own water provider's plan. Check the current stage, then ask the company you are connected with whether the job can go ahead now or should wait.

My Katy HOA sent a letter about a dirty fence. Who handles that?

First check whose fence it is. Some large associations maintain perimeter and common-area fencing themselves, so a letter about your own side fence is different from a problem with the wall along the main road. If it is yours, call the line and say it is a fence with an HOA deadline. The company you are put through to can look at the boards and tell you what cleaning will and will not change. See fence cleaning.

Is Cinco Ranch part of the City of Katy?

No. Cinco Ranch is a census-designated place in the City of Houston's extraterritorial jurisdiction, spread over Fort Bend and Harris counties, even though most people call it Katy. That matters for cleaning because water-use rules come from your own water provider, not the City of Katy, and exterior standards come from the Cinco Ranch associations' deed restrictions.

How long should a cleaned fence dry before I stain it in Katy?

Sherwin-Williams suggests about 24 to 48 hours after cleaning, and Behr says to let the wood dry completely, which may take about a day. In a humid stretch, or for boards that sit in shade, give it longer. The company that cleans the fence can tell you when the wood is ready, and deck and patio cleaning covers the same question for decks.
